known.title: A landing reconciled from a trunk report (T16) records no landed symbol changes and leaves the author's in-progress rows in_progress
known.claim: completeLanding with reconciled:true skips symbol_changes, while advance/resolve landed with symbol_changes [] supersede the author's in-progress rows, so the two landed paths disagree.
known.scenario: A landing found on trunk via a trunk report (T16) completes; GET /symbol-changes still shows the author's in-progress rows for that task as in_progress. Reported by the H6 step verifier and the CP3 checkpoint verifier.
known.design_ref: T16 ('landed effects as far as they still apply'), 2.5

known.title: The hub silently drops lander symbol_changes entries it cannot record
known.claim: Entries with a bad key or path, an unknown kind, or past 1000 are dropped with nothing logged or reported, so a hub/lander contract mismatch goes unnoticed.
known.scenario: The lander sends a symbol_changes entry with a key symbols emits but the hub rejects; the landed report succeeds and the change is silently lost.

known.title: queueView is recomputed for every landing returned and every event
known.claim: shownLanding and emitUpdated recompute queueView per landing and per event; listLandings is about 40% of the simulation's CPU, which makes the 2,000-seed simulation take about 160 s and the full test suite about 300 s.
known.scenario: Profile the lander simulation: listLandings dominates. Caching queueView per write() would make the simulation several times faster.

known.title: Fix-it reports find no hunks in CRLF files
known.claim: parseConflictMarkers does not recognise the '=======\r' separator, so a conflict in a CRLF file produces no hunks (and no hunk symbols) in the fix-it report, while conflictRegions in regions.ts handles CRLF.
known.scenario: git merge-file -p --diff3 on CRLF files emits CRLF markers; parseConflictMarkers returns no hunks for them.

known.title: resolveInDoubt reads trunk's symbols config from the current trunk tip instead of the landed commit's parent
known.claim: In resolveInDoubt step 2 the symbols section comes from the fetched current trunk, not from T0, so landed symbol changes can be computed under the wrong enabled/exclude settings.
known.scenario: symbols.enabled or exclude changes on trunk between the push and the in-doubt resolution.

known.title: Some landed symbol_changes paths in the lander have no test
known.claim: resolve {landed} after a stale push (pipeline.ts afterStale), the in-doubt 'already on trunk' path, and the rule that a no-op landing sends [] are untested; mutations there are not caught.
known.scenario: Remove symbol_changes from the afterStale resolve call: all tests still pass.

known.title: The simulation's mutation guards have no control runs
known.claim: Each mutation guard runs under its own tuned fault profile, and no control test shows that same profile staying green without the mutation, so a broken profile that always fails would still count as a catch.
known.scenario: Make a guard's fault profile itself violate an invariant: the guard test still 'catches' it.

known.title: claim with path#name misreads a not-yet-existing file as a declaration
known.claim: splitTarget splits at the last '#' when the suffix is a valid symbol key and the whole path doesn't exist, so `claim docs/a#b.md` for a file not created yet claims docs/a with symbol b.md.
known.scenario: hub claim 'docs/a#b.md' before creating that file.

known.title: A Write to a file missing from this worktree is told to use Edit
known.claim: editScope returns whole_file_write before checking whether the file exists, so the deny reason tells the agent to use Edit on a file it cannot Edit.
known.scenario: Another agent added src/x.ts and holds declarations in it; this agent's Write of src/x.ts (absent here) is denied with 'use Edit for the parts you change'.

known.title: hooks-symbols.test.ts depends on test order
known.claim: Later tests rely on claims and worktree state left by earlier it blocks, so running one test alone with -t fails or tests the wrong thing.
known.scenario: npx vitest run packages/adapter/test/hooks-symbols.test.ts -t 'denies the same function'

known.title: who_uses throws for declarations named like Object.prototype properties
known.claim: whoUses reads entry?.ids[name] on a plain object, so names like toString, valueOf, constructor or hasOwnProperty throw, and the tool error is reported as a hub error.
known.scenario: who_uses on a method named toString.

known.title: The feed's impact state survives a hub that comes back on a new database
known.claim: resetHistory() clears the buffer but not listing, impactJobs or impactTold, so new symbol.changed events are evaluated against the old database's changes until the new seq passes the old listing's seq.
known.scenario: Hub restarts on a fresh database; the agent's impact notices are wrong or missing for a while.

known.title: who_uses reports everything as free when the hub's claims cannot be read
known.claim: When the claims request fails or times out, whoUses treats the list as empty and says 'nobody else holds it: update it yourself', listing every place in callers_free. Unknown is not free.
known.scenario: Hub down or slow beyond the 2 s budget; who_uses tells the agent to edit callers other agents may hold.

known.title: The reference cache can be poisoned by a concurrent write
known.claim: Blob ids are taken for all candidates first and each file is read and parsed later, so a file changed in between gets its new content's identifier index stored under the old blob id, including in the committed index blob shared by other worktrees.
known.scenario: A file changes between blobIds() and refEntry(); later lookups for the old blob return the wrong identifiers.

known.title: The 'unacked first' impact order is not really tested
known.claim: In the test the acknowledged change is also the older one, so newest-first ordering alone passes; removing the isAcked comparator from sortImpacts still passes.
known.scenario: Mutation: drop the isAcked term in sortImpacts; tests stay green.

known.title: post-edit claims others are told of a signature change after an edit restores the signature
known.claim: When an edit brings a signature back to its original shape the hub withdraws the row, but post-edit still says 'you changed the signature ... X holds it and is told of your change ... Record the new shape with decide'.
known.scenario: Change login's signature, then change it back; the second post-edit text is wrong.

known.title: Pruning held markers after 7 days can hold the agent twice for one landing
known.claim: markHeld prunes G/agenthub/held/* by mtime after 7 days, but a landing can stay queued that long when no lander runs (R13), so it can hold the agent a second time, breaking 'at most once per landing'.
known.scenario: holdTurn on, landing L-7 queued 8 days with no lander; the next Stop holds again.

known.title: A symbol claim_conflict at land tells the agent to wait on the whole file
known.claim: When land is refused with claim_conflict over a symbol, the text names a hub_wait on the whole file rather than on the held symbol (path#Symbol).
known.scenario: Another agent holds src/auth.ts#login; land is refused; the advice is hub_wait files ['src/auth.ts'].

known.title: Two agents' feeds race to fetch trunk into the shared refs/remotes/origin/main
known.claim: Worktrees of one repository share refs/remotes/origin/main; both feeds fetch into it at once and one logs 'cannot lock ref'.
known.scenario: Two agents in worktrees of one clone; trunk moves; one feed logs a lock error.

findings.title: After a check, the lander runs git inside the check's worktree, so a check can make the lander process run its commands outside checkWrapper
An agent's change lands unapproved in a protected file that trunk renamed it into
A landing whose landed signature changes exceed the hub's 1 MB body limit stays stuck in pushing forever after its trunk push
A lander crashes (uncaught) on any git output longer than V8's maximum string; a >512 MiB file in a landing crash-loops admission
Quadratic outline and signature work: a modest file stalls mapping for minutes (lander loses its lease, edits blocked, commits hang)
Sync's HEAD compare-and-swap runs before the slow status and in-the-way checks, so a commit made in that window is dropped from the branch
One landing whose admit request the hub refuses (413, or 400/403 on a path) stops admission for every landing queued behind it
The approver token goes to whatever hub URL the checkout's agenthub.json names, and `hub cancel` sends it without a TTY
`hub approve` passes hub-supplied shas and refs into git argv unchecked: a hostile hub can write files or run commands on the approver's machine
A .gitattributes below the root is not protected, so a landing can change merge attributes without human approval
externalPushes: pause is bypassed by any hand-pushed commit that carries agenthub trailers, and nothing tests the pause
Protected paths whose names git stores in NFD get a content-free approval digest, so an approval carries over to any later content
hub approve / hub reject can never act on a stacked landing whose protected path the landing it waits for also changed
A conflict in many files produces a fix-it report over the hub's 512 KiB limit; the landing comes back as lander_error, and three in a row pause the project
A lander_error send-back counts against keepPlaceRetries, so infrastructure failures cost the agent its queue place
An approved resume runs the merge ladder and the AI resolver again, and can fail a parked candidate that already passed its checks
Cancelling or superseding a landing during its checks (or the resolver) does not stop it; the queue stays blocked until the step ends
parseMergeTree throws on submodule conflicts (git appends free-form advice), so such landings fail as lander_error forever
Sync moves submodule gitlinks without updating initialized submodules; land then tells the agent to commit, which reverts trunk's submodule bump
A reset --keep that fails part-way leaves the worktree half-synced; sync reports 'nothing changed', drops the backup ref and the hooks say nothing
A sync whose CAS refuses because HEAD moved reports needs_human and blocks every edit until a human runs `hub sync --recover`
Hold planning is quadratic in a landing's size, so a large land, supersede or admission stalls every hub write for seconds
Every landing write, status and stats call scans and sorts the project's whole landing history with every report
An author can't edit a file its own live landing holds once another agent queues for that file
DocCache evicts a document still in use; it stays cached with a deleted tree, so later lookups on that text fail or read freed WASM memory
Constructor signature changes never reach callers; who_uses reports no callers for a constructor
A lost compare-and-swap race (for example two landers pushing the same C) is classified `rejected`, which pauses the whole project
The hub's pushing gate merges requirements that share a kind and digest, so a second protected rule over the same paths is not enforced at the hub
The idle trunk watch scans from the control `next` returned before the attempt's own trunk report
GC can delete the land ref of a landing being submitted at that moment if its commit is more than a day old
On a hub with a lander token, any agent can post messages, tasks, decisions and symbol changes as lander/…
The AI resolver prompt puts the agent-chosen file path outside the nonce-tagged untrusted parts
A trunk report over 1 MB fails every attempt as lander_error and pauses landing
A foreign trunk commit with a malformed Agenthub-* trailer makes every trunk report fail, so every attempt fails as lander_error and landing pauses
Lander git isolation still reads the global and system gitattributes files, so merge attributes don't come only from trunk
An AI-resolved file loses the incoming side's mode change (chmod +x) because the splice uses trunk's mode
The lander's mirror is never garbage-collected; objects from every merge, candidate and fetch build up without limit
A multi-commit cherry-pick or revert in progress (sequencer) is not seen as a git operation by sync or land
Sync's fetch passes --no-write-fetch-head (git 2.29+), so on older git every sync is fetch_failed instead of the fast-forward fallback
Lossy UTF-8 decoding hides changes to non-UTF-8 bytes, narrowing admission holds and guard checks
Edits to code swallowed by a persisting contained parse error claim only the swallowing declaration
post-edit posts every signature change of a Write in one request; over 200 the hub rejects all of them
land sends paths the hub refuses and tells the agent the hub and CLI are 'probably different versions'
After a hub database reset the feed still keys landing notices by bare landing id, so the new database's L-n notices are dropped
hub_wait/landing_status tell whoever reads another agent's failed landing to fix 'your change' and land again
I4 (config from trunk) and the test-weakening warning (§4.1 #7, #8) have no test at the lander
Sync's HEAD and tracked-file compare-and-swap before reset --keep is never exercised
hub approve's digest-mismatch refusal and `hub lander resume`'s terminal checks have no test
The e2e gate command silently drops the Phase 3 scenarios when an internal dist file is renamed
Two hub_wait tests use fixed sleeps instead of waiting for the wait to begin, so on a slow machine they pass without exercising what they claim
